memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'The son who is to succeed him as anointed priest shall prepare it. It is the LORD's perpetual share and is to be burned completely. Every grain offering of a priest shall be burned completely; it must not be eaten.'" - Lev 6:22-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a difference that matters. When an ordinary Israelite brought a grain offering, the priest kept most of it and ate. When a priest brought his own, none of it was eaten. It all burned.

The priest got no benefit from his own offering.

That is a searching principle for anyone in Christian service. It is possible to make your devotion to God serve your position — to pray in ways that build your reputation, to give in ways that get noticed, to serve in ways that feed your standing.

God removed that possibility for the priest. His personal worship had to be pure loss to him.

Jesus taught this repeatedly. When you give to the needy, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing (Mtt 6:3). He warned about those who do everything to be seen by others (Mtt 23:5), and said that those who have already received human praise have received their reward in full (Mtt 6:2).

There is a simple test in this. Is there anything you do for God that nobody knows about? Any giving, praying, or serving that brings you no return whatsoever?

That part of your life burns completely. And God alone receives it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does my service to God quietly serve my own reputation?
2. What do I do for God that nobody but God knows about?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, purify my motives. Let there be parts of my life given to You that bring me nothing at all but Your pleasure. Amen.
